answer: In an agent economy moving nectar from an orchard to a wharf, each identity must keep 100 credits in escrow to receive a fixed daily trading quota, and reclaiming the bond takes 30 days. A thousand fake identities therefore require 100,000 credits locked up, not merely a thousand generated keys. Splitting identities cannot increase the quota available per credit, so scaling a sybil attack requires proportional capital and incurs financing costs during the lockup.
